ctx.x: Eddie Dawson. Is that your full name? That's my full name. Eddie J. Dawson. Joseph Dawson. Eddie Joseph Dawson. Okay, and today is April the 5th. April the 5th, yes.

And it's 1972. 1972. Just beginning. Yeah, my name's Dick Allen. Let's get everybody's name then. Norse Edigo. Osberg. And that's spelled A with a little O over it. Yes, yes. C-E-R-G. Osberg. I'm trying to pronounce it right. Yeah, that's right. I have a hard time with these Swedish names. I know, yeah. What I wanted to ask you about was some of these people, you know, that, that nobody, uh, might remember very much about, like, did you know, uh, Babu, I'm sorry, Bubu Valentin? He played the valve trombone, and…

Yeah, St. Catharines Hall was, uh, on Tulane Avenue near Howard. Uh-huh. Yeah, I was, uh, altar boy. I used to be altar boy, you know. And I was raised up in the Third Ward, you know. And, uh, I attended, I used to, I just, I went to school at St. Catharines Church. Oh, they had a school, and a church, and a hall? Yeah, they had a school. And a hall? A church and a hall, a school in the back. Uh-huh. And where did the people dance? We never had no dance there, now that's in Catharines. Oh, I thought, they had,…

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions Dick Allen stopped by; INTERVIEWEE responds to a question about King Oliver, not Dick Allen.

ctx.x: 325 North Johnson and this is Bill Russell and Ralph Collins is here and the date is June the 28th, 1961. Well, I think I would have, Dick Allen just stopped by and I said what can we ask Mr. Dawson? He said ask about the time that the King Oliver used to drop the brick or something.

What was that for? That was for the, to give you a notice to stop playing, you know. When you, the boys when they knock off, they keep on playing over, you know, couple of strings, couple of bars over the beat, over the knockoff and well, he just got a big brick and when he got ready to knock off he throw the brick down on the music stand and see I guess you'll hear that. He really did that, huh? Yeah, he did that. I don't think he was kissing. No, no, he did that, yeah.
